strings.name: Ryan Dahl
strings.role: Software engineer · Creator of Node.js and Deno
strings.summary: Ryan Dahl created Node.js, advancing JavaScript beyond browsers, and later developed Deno and related tools with a team. In October 2026 the Deno team joined Cloudflare, shifting development toward Workers-related infrastructure and announcing a runtime maintenance period and a Deno Deploy shutdown plan. These projects include collaborators and community contributions; he did not invent server-side JavaScript itself.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth information is limited to 1981, without an unverified month or day. Team membership, future maintenance termination and hosting shutdown plans are distinguished. Product security is not independently certified.
strings.influence.rationale: Created Node.js and Deno, advancing JavaScript use on servers and in modern application development.
strings.facts.f1.label: Key projects
strings.facts.f1.value: Node.js and Deno, both subsequently developed and maintained by teams and communities.
strings.facts.f2.label: Direction in 2026
strings.facts.f2.value: Joined Cloudflare to work on self-hosted applications using Workers and workerd.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Expanding JavaScript applications
strings.highlights.h1.text: Advanced server, command-line and application development through Node.js and Deno.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Rethinking runtime tools
strings.highlights.h2.text: Worked with teams on permission controls, TypeScript support and cross-runtime package tools.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Deno team joins Cloudflare
strings.timeline.t1.text: Announces a shared-platform focus, another year of runtime maintenance and a planned Deploy shutdown after six months; neither stops that day.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Introduces Deno Sandbox
strings.timeline.t2.text: His signed announcement describes Linux microVMs for untrusted code, network egress controls and secret protection; these are vendor descriptions.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Co-releases Deno 2
strings.timeline.t3.text: Releases a new version with collaborators, expanding Node.js/npm compatibility and project-management tools.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Announces JSR public beta
strings.timeline.t4.text: Introduces a TypeScript and ES-module package registry with Luca Casonato and Kevin Whinnery.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Co-releases Deno 1.0
strings.timeline.t5.text: Co-authors the release with Bert Belder and Bartek Iwańczuk, presenting a JavaScript/TypeScript runtime outside browsers.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Introduces Deno publicly
strings.timeline.t6.text: Presents Deno at JSConf EU in Berlin while reflecting on Node.js design choices.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Hands over day-to-day Node.js leadership
strings.timeline.t7.text: Transfers release decisions to Isaac Schlueter in a mailing-list post, remaining at Joyent and offering advice.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Creates Node.js
strings.timeline.t8.text: Develops and presents the JavaScript runtime, later advanced by a wider team and community.
